answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a wharf, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 408 aliases as a result costs 114 bonds held for 20 days each, plus the falcon attestations those aliases can never earn. A single lotus checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
